newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin orders PM to control arms exporter.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin orders PM to control arms exporter.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin on Tuesday put all foreign contracts by Russia's main arms exporter, Rosvooruzheniye, under the direct control of Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin, the Kremlin press service said.

Newspaper reports earlier this month featured accusations, denied by Rosvooruzheniye, that the agency made illegal arms sales and diverted proceeds to a secret fund for Yeltsin's re-election campaign last year.
A Rosvooruzheniye spokesman said a decree signed by Yeltsin removed certain bureaucratic obstacles for the agency and left "many issues" in Chernomyrdin's hands.
Rosvooruzheniye had always been a state agency under government control and the decree only changed certain details of handling its activities, the spokesman said.
Other Russian companies have charged Rosvooruzheniye with using aggressive tactics against domestic competitors, and some have complained that it amounts to a state monopoly.

Roosvooruzheniye has denied any wrongdoing and accused foreign and domestic rivals of waging a campaign to prevent it completing lucrative new contracts. It said it had built up its domination of the market by virtue of hard work.

Rosvooruzheniye is responsible for 95 percent of Russian arms sales and its exports in 1996 reached $3.5 billion. It has contracts worth $7 billion and hopes to increase that to $9 billion by the end of the year.
